raw_case_text:
A well-grown, normally developed, 11-year-old girl received a scheduled MR vaccine. After 2 days, she developed high-grade fever, followed by headache, drowsiness, irrelevant talk, urine retention, and generalized seizure over a span of 12 days. Her past history was insignificant. Suspecting infectious etiology, she received ceftriaxone, amikacin, and intravenous (IV) fluids. Her sensorium deteriorated, however; hence referred to tertiary care hospital.
She had fever, heart rate (HR) 120/min, respiratory rate (RR) 25/min regular, capillary refill time (CRT) 2 s, blood pressure (BP) 110/70, and SpO2 100% in room air. Other than central nervous system (CNS), all other systems were found to be normal. She was disoriented with low Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) (10/15) and positive meningeal signs. Her pupils, fundus, and cranial nerves examination was normal. Lower limbs had paucity of movements with absent deep reflexes as compared with upper limbs, with loss of abdominal and plantar superficial reflexes. Fundus examination was normal. Initial investigations showed hemoglobin (Hb) 12.6 gm, total leukocyte count (TLC) 27,750/cmm, neutrophil (N) 87%, lymphocyte (L) 10%, platelet 4.02 l/cmm, normal renal function test (RFT), liver function test (LFT), electrolytes, and blood gas. Rickettsia and dengue serology were negative. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) showed 700 cells/cmm, L 70%, protein 156 mg/dl, and glucose 56 mg/dl [body sugar level (BSL) 104] with normal lactate. Serum ammonia and antinuclear antibody (ANA)/double stranded DNA (DsDNA) were normal. Electroencephalogram (EEG) showed background slowing without electrographic seizures. CSF polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panel [herpes, chickenpox, cytomegalovirus (CMV), Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), enterovirus, para-echo, mumps, and rubella], gram/Zn stain, bacterial antigen latex agglutination, and cultures were negative. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain with spine revealed leptomeningeal enhancement and non-specific white matter hyperintensities with normal spine. We continued empirical IV antibacterial, antiviral, and supportive care awaiting investigations.
Child worsened within 2 days, however; child had no vocalization, no eye opening, and no motor response needing mechanical ventilation. Repeat MRI surprisingly showed diffuse non-enhancing hyperintensity in entire spinal cord and brain stem without any signal in optic nerves (Figure 1). Repeat CSF showed 30 cells/cmm, L 95%, proteins 44 mg/dl, and glucose 60 mg/dl. Demyelination panel revealed high immunoglobulin G (IgG) and positive anti-MOG and negative neuromyelitis optica (NMO) antibodies; for which we administered IV immunoglobulin and IV methylprednisolone. Her sensorium, walking, and bladder control improved over 10 days, 4 weeks, and 6 weeks, respectively. She was discharged on oral steroids.
A fortnight later, steroids were unintentionally stopped by parents, and she came back with complete visual loss. She was only perceiving hand movements and could not count fingers from 1 feet distance. Her clinical evaluation showed normal sized sluggishly reacting pupils without relative afferent papillary defect (RAPD). Visual evoked potential (VEP) was delayed with fundus examination showed papillitis confirming bilateral optic neuritis (ON) without other neuro-deficit. We escalated immunotherapy to rituximab, continued steroids for 6 months with slow tapering. During last 3 years follow-up, she is asymptomatic, with intact intelligence and vision with no neuro-deficit or seizure. Written and informed consent of the parents have been taken.

subjective.chief_complaint: An 11-year-old girl presented with a 12-day history of high-grade fever, headache, drowsiness, irrelevant speech, urinary retention, and generalized seizures beginning 2 days after measles-rubella (MR) vaccination, followed 2 weeks after steroid discontinuation by acute bilateral blindness.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Two days after receiving a scheduled MR vaccine, the previously healthy girl developed high-grade fever, headache, progressive drowsiness, irrelevant talk, urinary retention, and generalized seizures over 12 days despite empiric ceftriaxone and amikacin, progressing within 2 days of tertiary admission to coma requiring mechanical ventilation. Two weeks after her parents unintentionally stopped her post-discharge oral steroids, she represented with acute bilateral visual loss (hand movements only).
subjective.past_medical_history: Normally developed 11-year-old girl; received scheduled measles-rubella (MR) vaccine 2 days prior to symptom onset; insignificant past medical history.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for high-grade fever, headache, drowsiness, irrelevant speech, urinary retention, generalized seizures, lower-limb weakness, and subsequent acute bilateral visual loss.

objective.physical_examination: On admission: febrile, HR 120/min, RR 25/min, CRT 2 s, BP 110/70 mmHg, room-air SpO2 100%, disoriented with GCS 10/15, positive meningeal signs, normal pupils/fundus/cranial nerves, and lower-limb paucity of movement with absent lower-limb deep tendon, abdominal, and plantar reflexes; deteriorated within 2 days to coma (no eye opening, vocalization, or motor response). At relapse 2 weeks after stopping steroids: vision reduced to hand movements at 1 foot bilaterally, sluggishly reactive normal-sized pupils without RAPD, and bilateral optic disc papillitis on fundoscopy.
objective.routine_investigations: Admission labs: Hb 12.6 g/dL, TLC 27,750/cumm (87% neutrophils, 10% lymphocytes), platelets 4.02 lakhs/cumm, and normal RFTs, LFTs, electrolytes, ABG, ammonia, ANA, and anti-dsDNA. Rickettsia serology was negative. EEG showed diffuse background slowing without epileptiform discharges; visual evoked potentials (VEP) at relapse showed delayed latencies bilaterally. Serum demyelination panel revealed elevated IgG, positive anti-myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein (anti-MOG) antibodies, and negative anti-NMO (aquaporin-4) antibodies.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial CSF showed 700 cells/cumm (70% lymphocytes), protein 156 mg/dL, glucose 56 mg/dL (blood glucose 104 mg/dL), normal lactate, and negative Gram/ZN stains, bacterial antigen latex agglutination, cultures, and viral PCR panel (HSV, VZV, CMV, EBV, enterovirus, parechovirus, mumps, rubella); repeat CSF showed 30 cells/cumm (95% lymphocytes), protein 44 mg/dL, and glucose 60 mg/dL. Initial brain/spine MRI showed leptomeningeal enhancement and nonspecific cerebral white matter hyperintensities; repeat MRI on day 3 revealed diffuse non-enhancing T2 hyperintensity throughout the entire spinal cord and brainstem.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Post-MR-vaccination anti-MOG antibody-associated encephalomyelitis (longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis and brainstem encephalitis) with multiphasic relapse as bilateral optic neuritis, confirmed by positive anti-MOG antibodies, spine/brainstem MRI, and VEP. Dengue was ruled out by negative dengue serology. Treated initially with mechanical ventilation, IVIG, and IV methylprednisolone (recovering sensorium in 10 days, ambulation in 4 weeks, and bladder control in 6 weeks), and escalated at optic neuritis relapse to rituximab plus a 6-month oral corticosteroid taper, maintaining complete visual and neurological remission over 3 years of follow-up.
